chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Paul Whiteman's poll and Eldridge's Savoy booking
summary: Willard asks whether Whiteman's Saturday Evening Post jazz poll mattered; Collins says it brought Roy work commercially, including the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: You said that Paul Whiteman had
proclaimed Roy Eldridge the greatest trumpet player in the United States.
At that time was Paul Whiteman the ultimate authority? I mean, you said that that resulted in a booking at the Savoy.

Yeah, yeah. Well, he was doing -- I think they were having the jazz poll, and this was -- of all things I really believe this was a Saturday Evening Post which figures, you know, Paul Whiteman would be with the Saturday Evening Post, you know.

Now, that's -- Dizzy said this in his act, and it was so appropos. You know, (he said) you know his name wasn't Paul Blackman. But any way it was in the Saturday Evening Post, it was like a jazz poll and he was allegedly an authority on jazz, you know. But any way --
Commercially it was quite a thing.
this made a lot of work for Roy?
And the Savoy booking was the result of Paul Whiteman?7
That's right. Well, you know, they read --
-- the Saturday Evening Post also, you know, and that was just another of the polls that Roy had won, you know, jazz polls. But this one coming from Paul Whiteman was quite an honor, you know. Yes.
